answer: One defense is correlated-behavior clustering with slashing. All votes are logged in a public atlas, and a cipher-based commitment scheme hides each vote until reveal, so copies cannot coordinate in real time. When many identities always vote identically and arrive together, like cargo unloaded at the same wharf, the system flags the cluster, demands fresh independent proof of work from each member, and slashes the deposits of those that fail. A Sybil farmer must therefore make every fake behave differently and pay for real work, instead of cloning one voting pattern for free.
